title: Get started with pipeflow
text: easier understanding, go step step. First, create new pipeline name “-pipeline” add data step provides input dataset. step, minimum specify name step (step = "data) function (fun) defines computed step. Let’s take first look pipeline. step represented one row table, currently shows four columns: step name step params names function parameters depends dependencies step () state state step, initially always set new Next, want add step called prep, prepares original data adding new column "Temp.Celsius". means, prep step use output data step. refer output earlier pipeline step, just write name preceded tilde (~) operator, case means ~data. Since pip_add works “reference”, can add step follows: reiterate: function(df = ~data) basically means function gets called df contain whatever produced last data step. , second step called prep added depends data step, also marked 2nd row column depends. Next, want add step called fit fits linear model data. function using prepared data defines parameter xVar, determines variable used predictor linear model. Lastly, add step called plot, plots data linear model fit. function references fit prep step. previous step, defines xVar parameter plus two plot-specific parameters xLab title. depends column row 4:, see plot step depends fit prep step. addition tabular output, {pipeflow} also provides graphical representation compatible visNetwork package. pip_graph() function returns list arguments can feed directly visNetwork::visNetwork(). , pipeline visualized directed acyclic graph (DAG) nodes represent steps edges represent dependencies.

32) * 5 / 9         df     } ) pip # <pipeflow> my-pip (2 steps) # --------------------------- #    step params depends state # 1: data   data           new # 2: prep     df    data   new # --------------------------- # <ready> last run: never pip |> pip_add(     "fit",     function(data = ~prep,              xVar = "Temp.Celsius") {         lm(paste("Ozone ~", xVar), data = data)     } )  pip # <pipeflow> my-pip (3 steps) # --------------------------- #    step    params depends state # 1: data      data           new # 2: prep        df    data   new # 3:  fit data,xVar    prep   new # --------------------------- # <ready> last run: never pip |> pip_add(     "plot",     function(model = ~fit,              data = ~prep,              xVar = "Temp.Celsius",              xLab = "Temperature in degrees Celsius",              title = "Linear model fit") {         require(ggplot2, quietly = TRUE)         coeffs <- coefficients(model)         ggplot(data) +             geom_point(aes(.data[[xVar]], .data[["Ozone"]])) +             geom_abline(intercept = coeffs[1], slope = coeffs[2]) +             labs(title = title, x = xLab)     } ) pip # <pipeflow> my-pip (4 steps) # --------------------------- #    step                     params  depends state # 1: data                       data            new # 2: prep                         df     data   new # 3:  fit                  data,xVar     prep   new # 4: plot model,data,xVar,xLab,title fit,prep   new # --------------------------- # <ready> last run: never library(visNetwork) do.call(visNetwork, args = pip_graph(pip)) |>     visHierarchicalLayout(direction = "LR")
